How to read this website

Was she really “the first programmer”?

She is often called that, particularly because of her published Note G from 1843. The precise claim to being first depends on what we mean by a program and publication; Babbage also produced earlier unpublished procedures. Her importance lies not just in the headline, but in explaining the machine's wider possibilities. Historical context ↗

What did we invent on this website?

TeaScript, Steam Cloud, Salon Undo, the AI beach images, the modern CV, cover letters and all contemporary quips. They are labelled as fiction. We do not attribute invented endorsements or job offers to anyone.

Where does the portrait come from?

A historical watercolour from around 1840 attributed to Alfred Edward Chalon. The reproduction is listed as public domain on Wikimedia Commons. Origin, attribution and licence ↗
